tags.name: Exotic House Reef
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-08-21: confirmed as Malapascua Exotic Island Dive Resort's managed house reef, built up with artificial structures (jeepneys, concrete blocks) since 2001 and awarded Project AWARE's Environmental Achievement Award in February 2008 (scubatravel.com). Removed unsupported mandarin fish and blue-spotted ribbontail ray claims — mandarin fish sightings are only clearly source-confirmed at the Lighthouse site among our sources, not here.

tags.name: Lighthouse
tags.qa_note: MAJOR CORRECTION 2026-08-21: prior entry described Lighthouse as a 30m wall dive with hawksbill turtles and thresher sharks — depth, site_type, and difficulty were all wrong, and none of five independent operator sources support that content. Lighthouse is consistently documented as a shallow (5-10m) reef site famous for mandarin fish mating displays at dusk. All wall/turtle/thresher/shark content has been replaced with source-backed content. Note: this is a distinct site from the much deeper 'Japanese Ship Wreck' entry located nearby, which remains unresolved — do not conflate them.

tags.name: Monad Shoal
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-08-21: corrected working depth range to 16-30m (was 5-50m); the recreational cleaning-station platform sits in this range, though the surrounding seafloor drops much deeper (some operators cite technical depths beyond 30m for the plateau's edge — not asserted as a specific number here). An April 2025 ScubaBoard trip report confirms thresher sharks are still reliably sighted (~20 in one day) before boat traffic disrupted the site. Several current operator sources note thresher activity has partly shifted to nearby Kimud Shoal in recent years and that Monad is now also cited for occasional tiger shark sightings — both noted in the markdown. Softened hammerhead/manta claims to 'occasional, not guaranteed' per source language.

tags.name: Japanese Ship Wreck
tags.qa_note: UNRESOLVED, deep-researched 2026-08-21: two real, well-documented WWII Japanese wrecks exist near Malapascua, and this OSM entry's coordinates/depth do not cleanly match either. (1) 'Lighthouse Wreck' — a landing craft roughly 3-7m deep, broken in two, located ~5-10 min by boat right off the Malapascua lighthouse point (coordinates ~300m from this entry); sources conflict on sinking cause (bombed approaching the beach with a cement cargo per padi.com, vs. spotted while hiding from American forces per kokaysmalditodiveresort.com). (2) 'Tapilon Wreck' (tentatively identified by one source as possibly the Oakita Maru, unconfirmed) — a cargo carrier at 22-32m, hit by torpedoes, broken into 3 sections, located off Tapilon town roughly 30 minutes by boat from Malapascua — i.e. NOT near this entry's coordinates. This entry's depth (33m) is close to Tapilon's range but its coordinates sit at the Lighthouse location; no source resolves this contradiction. No Wikipedia article was found for either vessel. Per policy, no vessel name/history/marine-life claims are published until identity is confirmed. Needs human review — likely a coordinate or depth data-entry error on one of the two real wrecks, or these are two separate unlisted wrecks in the same OSM cluster.
